title: Shinagawa on Foot
blurb: Walk Shinagawa under the real sun: out of the Konan exit among the towers, up the tracks to Takanawa Gateway's folded roof, and south over the Yatsuyama bridge to the old Tokaido's post town.

npcs.name: Kenji 健司
idle: Eight in the morning, the passage to the Konan exit is a river of grey suits. There's a famous photograph of it.
The Shinkansen to Osaka stops here; the airport trains too. Everyone passes through Shinagawa. {time}.

npcs.name: Asuka 明日香
idle: Inside, the roof lets the daylight through. On a sunny day you don't need a single lamp.
The old embankment they found here was the first railway in Japan: 1872, on the sea. {sun_line}

npcs.name: Masa 雅
npcs.role: Sweet shop owner 和菓子屋
idle: Shinagawa-shuku: the first night out of Edo on the Tokaido. Inns, teahouses, and travellers saying goodbye.
My family has made sweets on this road for five generations. The road's older.

npcs.name: Kaori 香織
idle: An aquarium in a hotel: dolphins, a jellyfish room, and a tunnel of sharks.
At night the dolphin show has lights and music. Book ahead.

quests.title: Shinagawa
talk: Welcome to Shinagawa. Konan's towers along the canal this side, hotels and hills across the tracks.
Walk up to Takanawa Gateway, the new station. Asuka can show you around.

quests.title: Takanawa Gateway
talk: Look at the roof: white membrane on timber, folded.
The whole rail yard here is becoming a new town. Come back in ten years.

quests.title: Shinagawa-shuku
talk: The Tokaido, the old road to Kyoto. Walk along it a little.
Then go and see the dolphins up the hill, at the hotel. Kaori works there.

spots.name: Takanawa Gateway Station 高輪ゲートウェイ駅
lines: Takanawa Gateway, 2020: the Yamanote line's first new station in fifty years. Kengo Kuma folded its roof like origami.
They found the stone embankment of 1872 under the yard while building it: Japan's first railway ran on it along the shore.

spots.name: Shinagawa-shuku 品川宿
lines: The old Tokaido: the first post town out of Edo on the road to Kyoto. Travellers spent their last night in the city here.
The road is the same width it was in 1700. The shops are newer, mostly.
Nihonbashi that way, Kyoto that way. Five hundred kilometres. Mind the bicycles.
